### Authenticated preview proxy implemented (2026-10-23T14:48Z)

- **Decision:** the user chose the Neon-authenticated Worker proxy, preserving
  the existing Access protection and requiring no Cloudflare dashboard change.
- **Worker:** new `worker/src/preview-proxy.ts` plus shared contract
  `src/lib/preview-proxy-contract.mjs`. The API origin's
  `GET|HEAD /admin/preview/<pages-host>/<path>` verifies the active Neon
  session and membership, mints a one-hour host-bound HMAC token
  (`REVIEW_SIGNING_SECRET`), and redirects to the separate preview origin
  (`PREVIEW_ORIGIN`, the existing workers.dev Worker host). The preview origin
  exchanges the token for an HttpOnly `__ll_preview` cookie and serves the
  preview from that origin, fetching with the Access service token and
  rewriting same-site HTML/CSS/redirects. Browser probes proved that a CSP
  `sandbox` opaque origin blocks both session cookies on subresources and
  Astro module scripts, so isolation comes from the separate origin instead:
  generated-site scripts cannot reach admin APIs with the host-only Neon
  session. The preview cookie grants only preview access. Every non-preview
  path on the preview origin returns `404`, so generated-site scripts cannot
  reach Worker or admin APIs there even if a legacy host cookie exists. Only
  `*.launchloom-pipeline-preview.pages.dev` (or `PREVIEW_PROXY_HOSTS`) is
  fetchable; an unrelated `pages.dev` host is rejected before any service token
  is sent. Userinfo, ports and non-HTTPS targets are rejected. Missing service
  credentials fail closed with `502`, never the Access login page.
- **Links:** `scripts/preview-link.mjs` probes a developer preview and selects
  the proxy only when Access intercepts it. `send-preview-email.mjs` applies it
  to developer-facing audiences only; `run-pipeline-test.mjs` applies it to
  focused-test notifications; `src/admin/format.ts` `previewHref()` applies it
  to workspace preview links. Production links stay direct.
- **Deployment:** `deploy-platform.yml` installs
  `CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID`/`SECRET` as Worker secrets when present;
  workflow jobs receive `LAUNCHLOOM_ADMIN_ORIGIN` from `ADMIN_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`.
- **Docs:** new `docs/preview-access.md`; focused-test setup updated.
- **Focused validation so far:** `worker/test/preview-proxy.test.ts` 22 passed
  (including token exchange, cookie serving, preview-origin route isolation,
  host binding and routing); `tests/preview-link.test.ts` 12 passed;
  `tests/pipeline-test-runner.test.ts` + `tests/admin-view-model.test.ts` 87
  passed; `npm run check:worker` clean; `npm run check` 0 errors (5 pre-existing
  hints); `npm run build:admin` and `npm run build` completed.
- **PR:** [#186](https://github.com/WrazyAI/launchloom/pull/186) opened from
  `codex/launchloom-preview-auth` after rebasing onto `origin/main` `9e91ea94`.
  Commit `4df6d9f4`. No Cloudflare Access application or dashboard setting was
  changed.
- **Additional evidence:** the live link selector returns the proxy URL for
  `review-initial.launchloom-pipeline-preview.pages.dev` and the direct URL for
  the public Juniper Grove client preview. A developer-email envelope render
  (no send) contains
  `https://api.launchloom.wrazyos.com/admin/preview/review-initial.launchloom-pipeline-preview.pages.dev/?review=...`
  with no Access hostname; a client-email envelope stays direct. Browser
  probes proved a CSP-sandboxed document sends no session cookies for
  subresources and cannot load Astro module scripts; the separate-origin,

## 2026-10-23T17:00:00Z - Duplicate focus-state contrast finding fixed

- Root cause: `inspectContrastPage` re-measures every visible element in each focus/hover/open state. Before this fix, out-of-scope targets were intentionally not pixel-resolved in those states because the default state already proved them. The same `h2` therefore changed from a pixel-proven `pass` in the default state to a duplicate `unresolved` finding in the focus state, with identical paint and backdrop.
- Fix in `scripts/rendered-contrast.mjs`: `resolveRenderedBackdrop` now re-proves a target from state-local pixels when its only structural issue is `background plate only partially covers text`. Partially clipped targets are captured from their visible intersection with a fixed, non-scrolling page clip. Fully offscreen partial plates are captured only in the default state: scroll to a deterministic position, capture there, then restore the previous scroll, so fixed backgrounds are measured at the viewport origin the user would see. Non-default states omit fully offscreen partial plates because the default state is authoritative. Nothing is suppressed for any other issue class, no threshold changes, and out-of-scope targets with any other issue remain fail-closed.
- A first attempt used an identity-based dedupe of unchanged targets. Independent review reproduced gradient, overlay, and fixed-background false passes with that approach. It was committed as `9ec94125` and then superseded by `f8646574` before merge. The shipped fix never carries a default verdict into a state without a fresh pixel proof.
- Regression coverage in `tests/rendered-contrast.test.ts`: a partial plate that is pixel-proven in the default state must not return as an unresolved focus finding; an out-of-scope partial plate whose backdrop darkens on focus must still fail; and a focused control whose gradient darkens on hover must still fail.
- Validation:
  - `npx vitest run tests/rendered-contrast.test.ts`: 52/52 passed, including the three new tests.
  - `npm run verify:site-route-fixtures`: all three scenarios passed (`trades-static`, `care-static`, `trades-authored`), each with 8 routes, 30 browser profiles, technical/browser/contrast/local `pass`, `production`/`provider` `not_verified`, and zero real submissions. Exit 0.
  - Ten contrast and route suites: 169/169 tests passed across rendered contrast, pixel contrast, paint contrast, static homepage contrast, publish gate, template guard, route handoff, browser route verification, contrast sweep, and color contrast.
- Next: commit and ship this repair through PR CI, then rebase PR #187 onto the repaired main and rerun its checks.

## 2026-10-23T19:10:00Z - Re-review found and closed the clipped-target bypass

- Re-review confirmed the identity dedupe false passes are closed by `f8646574`: gradient hover, translucent overlay, and fixed-background scroll cases all fail again.
- It then reproduced a new bypass in the fully-visible bound: a partially clipped partial plate was dropped before resolution, so a black-on-black focus state passed. The final change keeps partially clipped targets and proves them from their visible intersection with a fixed page clip. Fully offscreen partial plates are omitted from non-default state findings because the default state already covers them. No partial-plate capture scrolls the page, and every other issue class remains fail-closed.
- Regression coverage now includes a partially clipped partial plate whose backdrop darkens on focus; it must fail. A separate test proves an offscreen fixed background at the target's scroll position. The fully visible duplicate, out-of-scope darkening, gradient hover, and fully offscreen policy tests remain.
- Final validation: `tests/rendered-contrast.test.ts` 55/55; all three route-fixtures scenarios pass with 8 routes and 30 browser profiles each and zero contrast findings; ten contrast and route suites 172/172 when run sequentially.
- Fully offscreen partial plates are a documented viewport policy: the default state remains authoritative and now captures them at a deterministic scrolled position with scroll restored. Non-default states do not re-measure them. Partially clipped and fully visible partial plates are re-proved from their visible intersection.
- Branch history: `9ec94125` identity dedupe (superseded), `f8646574` partial-plate re-proof (superseded), and the final follow-up commit with the non-scrolling observed-intersection capture. The final diff is what ships.
